name: Page translation
author: Mika
description: Translate a page open in Mika's browser into the language you want (Simplified or Traditional Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, or any other): it reads the page text, splits it at natural boundaries, translates chunk by chunk and shows the result against the original. Translation goes through your own OpenAI-compatible endpoint; the key comes from environment variables and never enters the conversation.

tools.name: translate
tools.description: Translate text into any target language. Accepts a page read verbatim and splits it into safe-size chunks itself; returns JSON with either `translation` (whole translated text) or, when no translation endpoint is configured, `segments` (numbered chunks) so you can translate them with your own model and label each part. Use it once per page, not once per paragraph. The user picks the language by asking (“translate into Traditional Chinese / English / Japanese”): pass their words through as `target`.

text.description: The text to translate. For a page, paste the page text here as-is (line breaks are fine). Long lists are fine: it keeps them chunked so a cheaper model still holds quality.

target.description: Target language, in the user's own words or a language code: Simplified Chinese (default), Traditional Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, German, Vietnamese, Arabic … Any language works. Pass what the user asked for; do not translate the language name into English unless they said so.

source.description: Source language when you know it (e.g. English, Japanese). Leave empty to let the translator detect it.

style.description: literal (close to the original wording) | polish (readability first) | default (accurate and natural).

chunk.description: Approximate characters per chunk before each model call, 200-6000, default 1800. Lower it when the source is dense.

tools.name: translate_languages
tools.description: Show how to choose the translation language (any language, spoken in the chat, plus the default via MIKA_TRANSLATE_TARGET). Call it when the user asks which languages are supported or how to change the default.

tools.name: translate_setup
tools.description: Show how to configure this plugin (which environment variables the translation endpoint needs) and whether it is configured now. Call it when the user asks how to set up translation, or when translate returns mode=segments and you want to tell them why.
